claims.text: The proposed RHEA is designed primarily from low-activation elements such as V, Cr, Ti, and Zr.
The proposed RHEA can serve effectively as a structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The proposed RHEA combines low neutron activation with enhanced high-temperature and irradiation resistance.
The as-fabricated RHEA has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
The as-fabricated RHEA has a balanced elemental distribution.
Temperatures above 1000 degrees Celsius are representative of the intended fusion plasma-facing-component environment.
The RHEA's single-phase BCC microstructure remains stable under the proposed fusion-relevant exposure conditions.
The high-entropy effect enables the stable single-phase BCC microstructure.
The stable high-entropy BCC microstructure suppresses deleterious phase segregation.
The stable high-entropy BCC microstructure suppresses deleterious precipitate formation.
The selected low-activation elements minimize formation of long-lived radioactive isotopes during neutron irradiation.
The high-entropy design enhances mechanical strength under extreme-temperature conditions.
The high-entropy design enhances irradiation resistance under extreme-temperature conditions.
The alloy will maintain microstructural integrity under fusion-relevant conditions.
The alloy will maintain mechanical performance under fusion-relevant conditions.
The alloy will exhibit lower neutron activation than tungsten.
The alloy will exhibit lower neutron activation than traditional vanadium alloys.
Tungsten suffers from high neutron activation in the stated application.
V-4Cr-4Ti has limited performance under combined high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Deviations from the intended elemental balance could cause phase instability or unexpected activation behavior.
